headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: B handles secrets and external APIs while A is a non-runnable docs-only list with no isolation or verification path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a docs-only awesome-list with no runnable surface, no filesystem, and no output channel that B would ingest by default. B has stdin/stdout and file I/O, but there is no documented bridge from A to B, so a prompt-injection pathway is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF A becomes a runnable agent whose outputs are piped into B's prompt or files, injection risk appears.
IF an orchestrator copies A-authored text into B without sanitization, B can be steered.
mitigations: Keep A as a non-executable reference artifact.
Do not feed A content directly into B prompts.
Add a manual review step before any copy-paste bridge.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any shared text channel.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B explicitly handles configuration secrets and uses allowlisted network egress, while A is a docs-only repo with no data classes touched. There is no shared workspace documented, so leakage is not proven, but B's secret-handling plus outbound API use makes accidental exposure plausible if A content is copied into B workflows.
conditions: IF A content is copied into B's notebooks or .env handling, secrets may be exposed.
IF B logs prompts or notebook cells containing copied A material, sensitive context can leak to external services.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in the same workspace as copied reference material.
Review notebook cells before execution.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately.
Disable outbound calls during manual review.
requires-engineering: separate secret storage from content-authoring workspaces.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. B can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but modify_git_state is false and no shared mutable target is documented. The only plausible conflict is if an operator manually points both at the same directory, which is unusual configuration.
conditions: IF both agents are manually pointed at the same writable directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF B is run with additional git-write tooling not shown in the profile, conflicts increase.
mitigations: Use separate working directories.
Keep A read-only.
Do not grant B git-write access unless needed.
Check for accidental path overlap before runs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B's course-style agentic RAG stack can act on retrieved content and uses APIs, while A is a reference list that could be treated as authoritative source material. If A's outputs are copied into B without verification, B may propagate stale or irrelevant claims into generated content or downstream actions.
conditions: IF A-derived text is inserted into B's retrieval corpus without validation, B may amplify errors.
IF B is configured to auto-generate answers from retrieved snippets, unverified A content can cascade.
mitigations: Verify A-derived facts before indexing them.
Mark A as non-authoritative in retrieval metadata.
Require citation checks before B outputs claims.
Sample outputs for hallucinated source attribution.
requires-engineering: add source-ranking and verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles configuration secrets and academic-paper data, while A is a public docs-only repository with no sensitive data classes. The main compliance concern is B's secret and paper-data handling under local development and allowlisted egress; A is not cited for a residency mismatch because none is documented. The pair creates a policy gap if A material is mixed into B's secret-bearing workspace.
conditions: IF EU paper data or secrets are copied into B's local development environment, retention and access controls must be enforced.
IF B's allowlisted egress sends paper metadata to third parties without a DPA, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared notebooks.
Document data-class handling for paper metadata.
Confirm third-party API terms before use.
Purge temporary files after runs.
requires-engineering: add retention and residency controls.
